about: Template for held-out grower-reply cases. Copy to evaluation/replies.local.json (excluded from git), replace the examples, and freeze the file before any run. Write cases without looking at REPLY_PROMPT in src/interpret.ts or earlier live outputs. Cases must be synthetic or used with permission; no real names or contact details.

Each case is a grower's first message, the coordinator's current reading of it, and the grower's reply. Only the reply is sent to the model to read; the reading is fixed so the run measures the reply step alone.

Standard synthetic hub: all lots grade standard, delivered Friday 2026-10-30. grower-a: lot-a tomato (kg), lot-c cucumber (kg). grower-b: lot-b tomato (kg), lot-d zucchini (kg). Replies come from the same grower as the message.

reading: operation (replace-total | add-quantity | forecast | unresolved), lotId, quantity {amount, unit: g|kg|each|case, pack?: {amount, unit: g|kg|each}}, grade, deliveryOn (YYYY-MM-DD). Use null for anything the message left open. Fields left open by the reading (for example operation unresolved, or cases without pack) are what the reply may answer.

label.answers: open fields the reply settles, with the value it states. label.open: open fields the reply does not clearly settle; they must stay open. label.corrections: fields the reading had settled that the reply explicitly changes, with the new value. Every open field must appear in answers or open; a settled field the reply merely restates is left out.
Values: operation is a string; lot a lot ID; quantity {amount, unit}; pack {amount, unit: g|kg|each}; grade a string; date YYYY-MM-DD.

Suggested coverage (aim for 3+ each, including clear replies so over-answering shows up): clear answer to every question; partial answer; vague or noncommittal reply ('yeah', 'should be fine'); explicit correction of a settled number ('sorry, 6 not 4'); restating a settled fact without changing it; unsupported or fractional units in the reply; reply about a different product or day; instruction-like text; informal or misspelled replies; replies answering in a different order or in one breath.

cases.message: Got 5 cases of standard zucchini for Friday.
cases.reply: Each case is about 4 kg, I'll check if that's on top of the earlier ones.
cases.note: 'about 4 kg' is an estimate, so pack stays open; the operation is explicitly unsettled.

cases.message: Another 3 cases of standard cucumbers for Friday.
cases.reply: Sorry, it's 2 cases not 3. 6 kg in each.
